title: GeneralizedSmoothAdam.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained differentiable objectives f: ℝ^d → ℝ, permitting nonconvexity, with f(x0) − inf_x f(x) ≤ Δ. No minimizer attainment is required.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each call at x returns g(x, ξ) using a fresh IID sample, with E[g(x, ξ)] = ∇f(x). The oracle supplies neither function values nor exact gradients. The jointly measurable oracle map and sampling distributions are hidden.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: For all x,y satisfying L1‖y−x‖ ≤ 1, ‖∇f(y)−∇f(x)‖ ≤ (L0+L1‖∇f(x)‖)‖y−x‖. L0,L1 ≥ 0; twice differentiability and samplewise smoothness are not required.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every x, E‖g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)‖² ≤ σ², with σ ≥ 0. Only second-moment control is imposed; bounded or sub-Gaussian noise is not assumed.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GeneralizedSmoothAdam.lean: spec.admissible, variance integrability and variance bound.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is Euclidean ℝ^d with its ℓ2 norm, for d ∈ ℕ.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: All Params are public, including L0,L1,σ,Δ,ε,x0 and β ∈ [0,1). Allowed algorithms belong to the supplied method family with this fixed β; ρ ∈ (0,1], η,τ,vinit > 0 and n ∈ ℕ may be chosen.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GeneralizedSmoothAdam.lean: Params, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.valid and spec.allowedAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm_squared
accuracy.details: The measurable output X must have integrable squared Euclidean gradient norm and satisfy E‖∇f(X)‖² ≤ ε², where ε > 0. The permitted method returns a saved iterate selected through its uniform random index.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: Expectation is over the independent algorithm seed and IID oracle stream. Oracle cost is a deterministic cap counting every gradient reply, not an expected stopping-time budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Gradient-dependent local smoothness extends the classical globally Lipschitz-gradient benchmark, while retaining IID unbiased bounded-variance gradients and expected squared-gradient accuracy.

descriptionHtml:
Adam under Generalized Smoothness

We consider minimizing a differentiable, possibly nonconvex function f:Rd→R, where d≥0 is an integer. The function f is (L0,L1)-smooth with L0,L1≥0, and a given starting point x0 satisfies f(x0)−infxf(x)≤Δ for Δ≥0. At x, the oracle returns an unbiased stochastic gradient with variance at most σ2, where σ≥0, using independent, identically distributed samples. We analyze Adam with positive initial second moments. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯ satisfying E∥∇f(x¯)∥2≤ε2, with expectation over sampling and algorithm randomness.

The optimization problem is infx∈Rdf(x), where ∥⋅∥ denotes the Euclidean norm. The algorithm receives d, the measurable sample space Ω, L0,L1,σ,Δ,ε, the starting point x0∈Rd, and a momentum parameter β∈[0,1).

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Generalized smoothness). The function f is differentiable everywhere, and for every x,y∈Rd, L1∥y−x∥≤1⟹∥∇f(y)−∇f(x)∥≤(L0+L1∥∇f(x)∥)∥y−x∥.

Assumption 2 (Initial objective gap). For every x∈Rd, f(x0)−f(x)≤Δ.

Assumption 3 (Stochastic gradient oracle). Let p be a probability measure on Ω. The oracle is represented by a jointly measurable map g:Rd×Ω→Rd. For every x∈Rd, the map g(x,⋅) is Bochner integrable, the squared error ∥g(x,⋅)−∇f(x)∥2 is integrable, and Eξ∼p[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),Eξ∼p[∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2]≤σ2. The sample sequence (ξt)t≥0 has a joint probability law Q on ΩN: its coordinate maps are measurable, mutually independent, and each has law p. At its tth query x, the oracle returns g(x,ξt). The algorithm’s randomness is independent of this sequence. Queries may be made at any point of Rd.

Our result is algorithm-specific: we analyze Adam with the following recurrence. The algorithm chooses constants 0<ρ≤1,η>0,τ>0,vinit>0,n∈Z≥0, using the available inputs. Starting from the given x0, it initializes m0=0 and vi0=vinit for i=1,…,d. Each query and update is gt=g(xt,ξt),mt+1=βmt+(1−β)gt,vit+1=(1−ρ)vit+ρ(git)2,xit+1=xit−ηmit+1vit+1+τ,i=1,…,d. The algorithm independently draws K uniformly from {0,…,n}. After an allotted budget of T∈Z≥0 oracle calls, its output is x¯={xK,K<T,x0,K≥T. Thus, when T≥n+1, the output is the uniformly selected queried iterate xK.

The required output is measurable, its squared gradient norm is integrable, and it satisfies EP[∥∇f(x¯)∥2]≤ε2, where P is the joint law of the independent selection K and sample sequence (ξt)t≥0.

• Shen-Yi Zhao, Yin-Peng Xie, Wu-Jun Li. On the convergence and improvement of stochastic normalized gradient descent. 2021. Complexity: O((1+L0Δ/ε2)(1+σ2/ε2)) stochastic-gradient oracle calls, including minibatches, for SNGD to achieve E∥∇f(X)∥≤ε; L0,L1,σ>0 and ε≤cL0/L1, with universal c>0.
  • Amirhossein Reisizadeh, Haochuan Li, Subhro Das, Ali Jadbabaie. Variance-reduced Clipping for Non-convex Optimization. 2023 preprint, v2; published ICASSP 2025. Complexity: O((1+L0Δ/ε2)(1+σ2/ε2)) stochastic-gradient oracle calls, including minibatches, for ClippedSGD to achieve E∥∇f(X)∥≤ε; L0>0 and ε≤cL0/L1, with universal c>0 and no such restriction when L1=0.

comparisonHtml:
Differentiable f:Rd→R, f(x0)−inff≤Δ, and ∥∇f(y)−∇f(x)∥≤(L0+L1∥∇f(x)∥)∥y−x∥ whenever L1∥y−x∥≤1. The jointly measurable oracle uses IID samples, is unbiased, and satisfies E∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2≤σ2; L0,L1,σ,Δ≥0, ε>0. The setup requires uncorrected coordinate Adam with prescribed β∈[0,1) and a uniformly selected pre-update iterate X. The target is E∥∇f(X)∥2≤ε2, over sampling and output randomization.

Adam under GeneralizedSmoothAdam.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) ExpectedGeneralizedSmoothAdam (Ours) (⋆⋆) (review) O(A(1+σ2)ε4+11−β)
(2) Adam (Jin et al. 2026), Thm. B.2; 0<p<1 O(1+d2ε4[1+log+⁡dε]2) Remaining parameters fixed; polynomial factors not displayed. Expected RMS; no p=1 guarantee. (1): Scope extends the same Adam expectation guarantee to p=1, including f=cosh. On the overlap, removes horizon logarithms; no full-class rate comparison. (1) needs IID bounded variance instead of conditional, gap/gradient-dependent second moments; fixes damping 1 and v0=(1+σ2)1.
(3) Adam (Jin et al. 2026), Claim B.1; globally smooth special case O(1+d2P112[1+σ2ε4+1ε2]); expected RMS, damping 1, v0=(1+σ2)1. (1): Smaller explicit polynomial parameter powers on the globally smooth overlap; matches the ε−4 exponent. Constants are unoptimized. (1) requires IID noise; (3) permits conditional bounded variance.
(4) Adam (Jin et al. 2026), Thm. B.1; p=1 O(1+d2(1+log⁡(1/δ))2[1δε4+1ε2]) Remaining parameters fixed; polynomial factors not displayed. Average squared gradient ≤ε2 with probability 1−δ. (1): Expected RMS for one fixed run; (4) tunes steps to δ. Criteria differ; costs are not directly comparable. (1) needs IID bounded variance instead of conditional, gap/gradient-dependent second moments.
(5) Adam (Zhang et al. 2025), Thm. 2; global coordinatewise smoothness O(ε−4) for sufficiently small ε, other parameters fixed; mean gradient norm ≤ε. Parameter factors unextracted; 0<β1≤β2<1. (1): Local Euclidean instead of global coordinatewise smoothness (allows cosh); RMS instead of mean norm. No established cost comparison. (1) requires IID bounded variance; (5) allows conditional coordinatewise affine variance and uses damping inside the square root.
(6) NSGD-M (Hübler et al. 2024), Cor. 16; L1>0 O(1+S4ε4[1+log+⁡Sε]4); mean gradient norm ≤ε. Schedule uses L1; common C2 class. (1): RMS certificate. For the shared mean target, noise dependence is Aσ2 instead of σ4 up to logarithms when σ≥max{1,L1Δ,L0/L1}; total gain requires σ2≫A. (1) has dimension dependence and worse smoothness/gap powers (Δ12 versus Δ4); needs σ for initialization. Noise comparison concerns only (6)’s displayed schedule.

Abbr: Costs count individual stochastic-gradient calls. RMS means (E∥∇f(X)∥2)1/2; mean means E∥∇f(X)∥. log+⁡t=max{0,log⁡t} for t>0, and log+⁡0=0; δ∈(0,1) is failure probability. A=(d+1)2(1+L0+L1)10(1+Δ)12/(1−β)4, S=L1Δ+σ+L0/L1. In (2), p replaces the gradient power 1 in local smoothness, with coefficient Lp>0. In (3), L is a global gradient Lipschitz constant and P=1+(1−β)−2+Δ+∥∇f(x0)∥+L+σ2; compare with (1) at L0=L,L1=0. Global coordinatewise smoothness in (5) means |∂if(y)−∂if(x)|≤(L0/d+L1|∂if(x)|)∥y−x∥ for all x,y,i.

import LongTails.Setups.HeavyTailedAdam

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.GeneralizedSmoothAdam

open OracleTemplate

noncomputable def method {d : ℕ} (β ρ η τ vinit : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (x0 : Adam.Point d) :
    Algorithm (Adam.Point d) (Adam.Point d) (Adam.Point d) where
  Seed := Fin (n + 1)
  law := ⟨(PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin (n + 1))).toMeasure, inferInstance⟩
  State := Adam.State d
  initial k := ⟨k.val, 0, x0, 0, WithLp.toLp 2 (fun _ => vinit), x0⟩
  query s := (0, s.point)
  update := Adam.update β ρ η τ
  output s := s.saved

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  L0 : ℝ
  L1 : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  β : ℝ
  x0 : Adam.Point d

attribute [instance] Params.measurableΩ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance q := Adam.Point q.d → ℝ
  Query q := Adam.Point q.d
  Reply q := Adam.Point q.d
  Output q := Adam.Point q.d
  publicInput q := q
  valid q := 0 ≤ q.L0 ∧ 0 ≤ q.L1 ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧ 0 ≤ q.Δ ∧ 0 < q.ε ∧
    0 ≤ q.β ∧ q.β < 1
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (g : Adam.Point q.d → q.Ω → Adam.Point q.d)
      (p : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω)),
      LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
        (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k) (p : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
      O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
            law := P
            answer := fun _ (_, x) ω => g x ω } ∧
      (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
      (∀ x y, q.L1 * ‖y - x‖ ≤ 1 →
        ‖gradient f y - gradient f x‖ ≤ (q.L0 + q.L1 * ‖gradient f x‖) * ‖y - x‖) ∧
      (∀ x, f q.x0 - f x ≤ q.Δ) ∧
      Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
      (∀ x, Integrable (g x) p) ∧
      (∀ x, ∫ ω, g x ω ∂p = gradient f x) ∧
      (∀ x, Integrable (fun ω => ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 2) p) ∧
      (∀ x, ∫ ω, ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 2 ∂p ≤ q.σ ^ 2)
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => ‖gradient f (output ω)‖ ^ 2) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, ‖gradient f (output ω)‖ ^ 2 ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ q.ε ^ 2
  allowedAlgorithm q A :=
    ∃ (ρ η τ vinit : ℝ) (n : ℕ), 0 < ρ ∧ ρ ≤ 1 ∧ 0 < η ∧ 0 < τ ∧ 0 < vinit ∧
      A = method q.β ρ η τ vinit n q.x0

end LongTails.Setups.GeneralizedSmoothAdam
